title: BECE English Studies: Vocabulary & Register - English Studies - Antonyms
subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the word most nearly opposite in meaning to the bolded word:

The doctor described the patient's illness as **acute**.
questions.explain: In a medical context, an 'acute' condition appears suddenly and worsens quickly, whereas a 'chronic' condition develops slowly and lasts for a long time. Thus, 'chronic' is the antonym.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the word most nearly opposite in meaning to the bolded word:

The two neighboring communities have lived in perfect **harmony** for decades.
questions.explain: 'Harmony' means a state of peaceful existence and agreement. Its direct opposite is 'conflict', which means a serious disagreement or argument.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the word most nearly opposite in meaning to the bolded word:

The possession of **illicit** substances is a serious offense punishable by law.
questions.explain: 'Illicit' means forbidden by law, rules, or custom. The antonym is 'legal', which means permitted by law.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the word most nearly opposite in meaning to the bolded word:

An adult education program was introduced specifically to assist the **illiterate** members of the village.
questions.explain: 'Illiterate' means unable to read or write. Its antonym is 'literate' or 'educated'.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the word most nearly opposite in meaning to the bolded word:

Before the devastating industrial oil spill, the coastal waters were considered completely **pristine**.
questions.explain: In environmental terms, 'pristine' means in its original, unspoiled, or clean condition. Its antonym is 'polluted', which means contaminated with harmful substances.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the word most nearly opposite in meaning to the bolded word:

The driver's license was suspended indefinitely due to his incredibly **imprudent** decision to overtake another vehicle on a blind corner.
questions.explain: 'Imprudent' means not showing care for the consequences of an action; rash. Its direct antonym in the context of road safety is 'cautious' or careful.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the word most nearly opposite in meaning to the bolded word:

To survive the impending national lockdown, rural households were sternly advised to bulk-buy **non-perishable** food commodities.
questions.explain: 'Non-perishable' foods do not spoil rapidly and have a prolonged shelf life (like canned beans). The opposite is perishable ('easily spoilt'), like fresh meat or vegetables.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the word most nearly opposite in meaning to the bolded word:

The widespread **emancipation** of slaves in the late 19th century was universally celebrated as a towering victory for global human rights.
questions.explain: 'Emancipation' means the formal process of being legally or politically set free. Its antonym is 'subjugation', which refers to bringing someone under severe control or enslavement.
questions.subject: English Studies
